nodes.question: Comparing the source and edited images, is the woman’s jacket front more closed in the edit, and is it fully closed?
nodes.criteria: Compare the jacket’s front-panel position and overlap in the source versus the edit. complete: the panels meet/overlap so the jacket is fully closed. partial: the panels are visibly closer together or overlap more than in the source, but the jacket remains partly open. absent: the jacket is not more closed than in the source. Do not infer closure progress from pose, motion, or reduced visibility of an inner layer alone. unknown: pose, occlusion, or image ambiguity prevents a reliable comparison.
nodes.binding: Visual target: the woman’s jacket front panels. Compare their visible separation/overlap between source and edited images; do not use pose or inner-layer visibility as a proxy.

program.checker_template: Execute exactly the supplied visual check on the source and edited images. Follow its saved binding, criteria and dependency evidence. Do not invent edits or infer an expected overall answer. Return JSON status, concise image-grounded evidence, and confidence (a number from 0 to 1, or null if unavailable). Confidence is your reported confidence in this check's observation, not a calibrated probability. A requested fulfillment check uses complete/partial/absent/unknown. A support check uses pass/fail/unknown. A known negative supporting observation can inform a requested check; it is not automatically uncertainty. Use unknown when the evidence cannot establish the requested fact. Do not count supporting facts as completed edits. Assess only the supplied check, not the overall instruction label.
